speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing a psychiatric condition along with a new onset movement disorder. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me the specific symptoms you are noticing with your movements and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very clear history; the improvement in your psychiatric symptoms is excellent. Now, regarding your new movement disorder, can you describe exactly what you are feeling (such as stiffness, tremors, or involuntary movements) and how it affects your daily activities?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Hyperkinesia (specifically Akathisia) secondary to Risperidone.

The symptoms you described—inability to remain still, fidgeting, and repetitive leg crossing—are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotic medications like risperidone. Given your history of starting this medication two months ago and the concurrent improvement in your psychiatric symptoms, the clinical picture strongly supports this diagnosis. I do not need to order further tests to confirm this; we can proceed with adjusting your medication dosage. Is your restlessness severe enough that it is preventing you from sitting through lectures or sleeping at night?
